newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves $400 mln debt purchases by FIIs.
newsitem.headline: India approves $400 mln debt purchases by FIIs.

text.p: India, which last month permitted foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to launch 100-percent debt funds in the Indian market, has approved proposals for purchases worth $400 million, D.R. Mehta, chairman of the regulatory Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Tuesday.
"In the last about three weeks we have already cleared cases worth $400 million of government debt," Mehta told a business conference.

"One or two applications are pending for $500 million more. It is quite possible that if we get one or two applications more the ceiling of $1.2 billion prescribed for this year will be achieved within a few weeks," Mehta said.
He did not give other details.

Later, a SEBI official told Reuters that the FIIs which had been permitted to invest in debt included J. Henry Schroder, Credit Suisse Investment Management, Peregrine Capital, HSBC Asset Management and Chescor.
